content_html:
Cusco is not only the historical capital of Peru, it is also an epicenter of ancestral celebrations full of music, dance and spirituality. If you are planning to visit this city in June, get ready to live one of the most impressive cultural experiences in South America.

What are the Cusco Festivals?

The Cusco Festivals are a set of cultural, religious and traditional celebrations that take place mainly in the month of June. The most notable is the Inti Raymi, or Festival of the Sun, an Inca ceremony that honors the Sun god on the Andean winter solstice.

During this month, the streets are filled with parades, comparsas, typical dances and activities organized by communities, educational institutions and cultural organizations. Cusco is transformed into a great living stage.

How to get to Cusco

There are several ways to get to Cusco, depending on your starting point:

  • airplane: Daily flights from Lima, Arequipa, Juliaca or international destinations such as Bogotá, New York among others.
  • Interprovincial bus: From Lima, Arequipa, Puno or Abancay. It is cheap, but the journey is long (10 to 24 hours).
  • Car trip: A more adventurous option, ideal for those who want to explore the Andean landscape.

Tip: For these dates, book in advance. Tourism increases a lot in June.

Best times to visit

Although Cusco is a tourist destination all year round, if your goal is to experience its festivities, the best time is:

  • June: Main month of celebrations.
    • June 5-7: Corpus Christi
    • June 23: Entrance to Qhapaq Qolla and Qhapaq Ch’unchu
    • June 24: Inti Raymi
  • Weather in June:
    • dry season
    • Pleasant temperatures during the day, cold at night
    • Clear skies ideal for photos

Tips to enjoy your trip

Here are some practical tips to take advantage of your visit:

  • Wear warm clothes: The nights are cold, even if there is sun during the day.
  • Hydrate and rest: The height can affect you the first few days.
  • Buy tickets in advance: For Inti Raymi and special tours.
  • Bring your camera or cell phone charged: There are many photo opportunities.
  • Check the official calendar: This way you don't miss any important parade.
  • Have cash on hand: In markets and fairs, many do not accept cards.
  • Explore by walking: Many streets are closed to vehicles during parties.

Conclusion

The Cusco Festivals are much more than a tourist event: they are a direct connection with the living history of Peru. Each dance, typical costume and ceremony has a deep meaning and reflects centuries of Inca and mestizo tradition. If you can visit in June, do it. You will have a transformative experience.
